system.name: Routable PCIe fabric
system.one_liner: an empirical study characterizing how routable PCIe fabrics connecting host servers to disaggregated device chassis share bandwidth

content.key_idea: Two hosts and two remote FPGA chassis share a routable PCIe fabric; flows sharing a host adapter, switch, or endpoint adapter (a) are compared against orthogonal flows under one root complex (b), while (c) shows a port lane/arbiter/credit-engine structure.
content.reading_order: Left pair of panels (a) interleaved and (b) orthogonal path-sharing scenarios across the same Server-Switch-Chassis topology, then the smaller inset (c) detailing one port's lanes and credit engine.

encoding.emphasis: drawing the identical Server-Switch-Chassis topology twice (a, b) with only the highlighted flow pattern changed isolates the effect of interleaved vs. orthogonal path sharing

We consider a small deployment with two host servers and two remote chassis, connected via an external PCIe switch

summary: This figure documents a small routable-PCIe testbed used to study in-fabric traffic sharing. Two host servers, each with a CPU, Root Complex, and Host Adapter, connect through an external PCIe Switch to two Remote Chassis, each exposing two FPGA endpoints through an Endpoint Adapter. Panel (a) shows an interleaved-path scenario where flows F1-F4 are configured so pairs of them share a host adapter (F1 vs F2), the switch (F1 vs F3), or an endpoint adapter (F2 vs F4), letting the authors measure how bandwidth is partitioned when paths interleave. Panel (b) repeats the same topology for orthogonal paths issued under the same root complex. Panel (c) is a smaller, generic port-architecture inset: SerDes/Retimer lanes (Lane 1 .. Lane n) in each of the Upstream and Downstream directions feed their own round-robin arbiter, and both arbiters feed a shared Credit Engine, illustrating the port-level mechanism underlying the fabric's bandwidth allocation.

notes: layout-proposal: paired-scenario-plus-inset — two structurally identical topology panels (a, b) contrasted only by which flows are highlighted, plus an unrelated small port-architecture inset (c); two-panel captures the (a)/(b) comparison but not the added inset, and no retrieved text describes panel (c) directly.
